Whenever my code fails with an unexpected bug, I feel stuck staring at the screen. What is a structured way to debug it?

Try narrowing down the problem in four calm steps: 1) Reproduce the bug reliably with the smallest possible input. 2) Read the exact error message and line number instead of guessing. 3) Verify assumptions — print or inspect actual variable values right before the failure. 4) Change only one thing at a time so you know what fixed it.

Why do filmmakers still shoot at 24fps when 60fps exists?
24 frames per second introduces natural motion blur that viewers traditionally associate with cinema. It also lowers data requirements per second compared to 60fps.
When is 60fps actually better then?
60fps works better for fast sports action, screen recordings of software tutorials, and slow-motion edits where you later slow playback down to 24fps or 30fps without choppiness.
Does doubling that double my exported file size automatically?

Not always automatically. Inter-frame video codecs reuse identical background pixels across frames, though at constant quality targets a 60fps export usually requires around 35 to 60 percent higher bitrate than 30fps.
